problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(\mu ,{15}^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-5\mu <X<7\mu )=0.5762,$ determine $\mu .$

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7580\,$ | $\,0.7611\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7881\,$ | $\,0.7910\,$ | $\,0.7939\,$ |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8159\,$ | $\,0.8186\,$ | $\,0.8212\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $-5\mu <X<7\mu $ is symmetric about the mean $\mu .$*
worked_solution:
Note that we can write the given probability as

$$
P(\mu -6\mu <X<\mu +6\mu )=0.5762,
$$

which tells us that the interval $-5\mu <X<7\mu $ is symmetric about the mean $\mu .$

First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mu -6\mu <X<\mu +6\mu ) & =0.5762 \\ 2P(\mu <X<\mu +6\mu ) & =0.5762 \\ P(\mu <X<\mu +6\mu ) & =0.2881 \\ P(X<\mu +6\mu )-P(X<\mu ) & =0.2881 \\ P(X<\mu +6\mu )-0.5 & =0.2881 \\ P(X<\mu +6\mu ) & =0.7881 \\ P(X\le \mu +6\mu ) & =0.7881 \\ P(X\le 7\mu ) & =0.7881\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 7\mu ) & =0.7881 \\ P(Z\le \frac{7\mu -\mu }{15}) & =0.7881 \\ Φ(\frac{6\mu }{15}) & =0.7881 \\ \frac{6\mu }{15} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7881) \\ \frac{2\mu }{5} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7881)\end{aligned}
$$

 

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.8)=0.7881\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.7881)=0.8.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\mu }{5} & =0.8 \\ 2\mu  & =4 \\ \mu  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
